title: 方案要拿到会上讨论，怎样请同事提前打磨？
topic: 请同事评阅提案，并明确希望他们检查的部分

source.title: 2017 Letter to Shareholders
source.type: 股东信公开介绍的内部备忘录工作方式
source.context: Amazon 官方公开业务资料。
paragraphs: We don’t do PowerPoint (or any other slide-oriented) presentations at Amazon. Instead, we write narratively structured six-page memos. We silently read one at the beginning of each meeting in a kind of “study hall.” Not surprisingly, the quality of these memos varies widely. Some have the clarity of angels singing. They are brilliant and thoughtful and set up the meeting for high-quality discussion. Sometimes they come in at the other end of the spectrum.

In the handstand example, it’s pretty straightforward to recognize high standards. It wouldn’t be difficult to lay out in detail the requirements of a well-executed handstand, and then you’re either doing it or you’re not. The writing example is very different. The difference between a great memo and an average one is much squishier. It would be extremely hard to write down the detailed requirements that make up a great memo. Nevertheless, I find that much of the time, readers react to great memos very similarly. They know it when they see it. The standard is there, and it is real, even if it’s not easily describable.

Here’s what we’ve figured out. Often, when a memo isn’t great, it’s not the writer’s inability to recognize the high standard, but instead a wrong expectation on scope: they mistakenly believe a high-standards, six-page memo can be written in one or two days or even a few hours, when really it might take a week or more! They’re trying to perfect a handstand in just two weeks, and we’re not coaching them right. The great memos are written and re-written, shared with colleagues who are asked to improve the work, set aside for a couple of days, and then edited again with a fresh mind. They simply can’t be done in a day or two. The key point here is that you can improve results through the simple act of teaching scope – that a great memo probably should take a week or more.

Beyond recognizing the standard and having realistic expectations on scope, how about skill? Surely to write a world class memo, you have to be an extremely skilled writer? Is it another required element? In my view, not so much, at least not for the individual in the context of teams. The football coach doesn’t need to be able to throw, and a film director doesn’t need to be able to act. But they both do need to recognize high standards for those things and teach realistic expectations on scope. Even in the example of writing a six-page memo, that’s teamwork. Someone on the team needs to have the skill, but it doesn’t have to be you. (As a side note, by tradition at Amazon, authors’ names never appear on the memos – the memo is from the whole team.)
translations: 在 Amazon，我们不开幻灯片式演示，而是写结构清晰的六页叙述型备忘录。每次会议开始时，大家会先默读。备忘录的质量差异很大：好的文档清晰、有思考，能为高质量讨论做好准备。
倒立的例子很容易说明什么是高标准：一套完成得好的动作有哪些要求，可以详细列出来，是否做到也很直观。写作则不同，优秀与普通备忘录之间的差异更难说清。尽管很难把优秀备忘录的详细标准写下来，读者往往仍会对优秀之处有相似感受。标准确实存在，只是不容易描述。
我们总结发现，备忘录写得不够好，往往不是作者看不出高标准，而是对工作范围和时间的预期不对：他们误以为一两天、甚至几小时就能写完一份高标准的六页备忘录，实际上可能要一周或更久。这就像想在两周内练好倒立，而团队也没有给予合适指导。优秀的备忘录会反复撰写和修改，请同事阅读并协助改进，放几天后再以新的视角编辑；一两天内很难完成。关键是帮助大家合理估算工作范围，明白写好一份备忘录可能需要一周甚至更久。
除了认识高标准并对工作范围有现实预期，还需要什么技能？写出世界级备忘录是否必须是顶尖写作者？作者认为，在团队协作中未必如此。足球教练不一定会传球，电影导演不一定会表演；但他们都需要识别相关领域的高标准，并教团队合理估算工作范围。六页备忘录也是团队工作：团队里需要有人具备写作技能，但不一定非得是你。（按照 Amazon 的惯例，备忘录不署个人姓名，而是代表整个团队。）

source.excerptReason: 选取备忘录的会议使用方式、评阅标准、反复修改及团队协作段落，练习请同事针对提案的具体部分给反馈；股东信其他段落与本课请求同事评阅的目标无直接关系。

notes.explain: memo 是用于讨论或决策的内部书面材料。
notes.example: I’m preparing a six-page memo for the product review.

notes.phrase: shared with colleagues who are asked to improve the work
notes.meaning: 与同事分享并请他们改进
notes.explain: ask someone to improve the work 是请同事直接帮助完善内容。
notes.example: I’ve shared the draft with two colleagues for feedback.

notes.meaning: 对工作范围有现实的预期
notes.explain: scope 指工作内容和所需投入的范围。
notes.example: Let’s agree on the scope before we set the review date.

scenario.title: 模拟情境：新产品方案下周要评审
english: You are preparing a product proposal for next week’s review.
The customer problem and recommendation are drafted, but you are unsure whether the scope and evidence are clear.
Ask a colleague to review specific sections before the meeting.
chinese: 你正在准备下周评审的新产品方案。
客户问题和建议已经写好，但你不确定工作范围和依据是否清楚。
请同事在会议前检查指定部分。

firstAttempt.prompt: 新产品方案下周要评审。请给同事发一条英文消息，请对方提前读客户问题和建议部分，并说明你最希望得到哪方面的反馈。
firstAttempt.sample: I’m drafting the product proposal for next week’s review. Could you read the customer problem and recommendation by Thursday? I’d value your feedback on whether the scope is realistic and the evidence supports the decision.
firstAttempt.rationale: 给出文档、需要反馈的部分和希望检查的标准。

words.example: I’m writing a memo to explain the launch decision.
words.translation: 我正在写一份备忘录，说明上市决定。

words.example: The project scope is too broad for a one-week review.
words.translation: 这个项目范围太大，一周内无法完成评审。

words.example: We revised the proposal after the customer interview.
words.translation: 客户访谈后，我们修改了方案。

taskPhrases.meaning: 你能在……之前帮我看一下……吗？
taskPhrases.example: Could you review the recommendation before Thursday?
taskPhrases.translation: 你能在周四前帮我看一下建议部分吗？

taskPhrases.meaning: 我很希望听听你对……的意见
taskPhrases.example: I’d value your feedback on whether the scope is realistic.
taskPhrases.translation: 我很希望听听你对工作范围是否现实的意见。

taskPhrases.example: Does the evidence support the recommendation?
taskPhrases.translation: 这些依据能支持这项建议吗？

structure.original: The great memos are written and re-written, shared with colleagues who are asked to improve the work, set aside for a couple of days, and then edited again with a fresh mind.
analysis: written and re-written 强调反复修改。
shared with colleagues 说明同事参与改进。
with a fresh mind 表示隔一段时间再检查。
structure.transfer: The customer proposal is drafted. I’ll share it with the account team and revise the pricing section after their review.

rewrite.good: Would you have time to review the customer problem and recommendation by Thursday? I’d especially value your feedback on the scope and whether the evidence supports the decision.
rewrite.translation: 你能在周四前抽空看一下客户问题和建议部分吗？我尤其希望听听你对工作范围以及现有依据能否支持这项决定的意见。
rewrite.pattern: Could you review [section] before [time]? I’d value your feedback on whether [criterion] supports [decision].

cloze.prompt: Could you ______ the customer problem before Thursday?
cloze.why: review a section 表示检查文档中的某一部分。

cloze.prompt: I’d value your feedback ______ whether the scope is realistic.
cloze.why: feedback on 后面接反馈主题。
support 在这里表示为建议提供依据。

dictation.label: 听写 1
dictation.text: We don’t do PowerPoint (or any other slide-oriented) presentations at Amazon. Instead, we write narratively structured six-page memos.
dictation.why: 留意 Instead 如何连接两种会议材料，以及 narratively structured 对备忘录的描述。

apply.prompt: 你能在周四前帮我看一下建议部分吗？
apply.sample: Could you review the recommendation before Thursday?

dictation.label: 听写 2
dictation.text: They simply can’t be done in a day or two.
dictation.why: 留意 simply can’t 强调不能把高标准备忘录压缩到一两天内完成。

apply.prompt: 我很希望听听你对工作范围是否现实的意见。
apply.sample: I’d value your feedback on whether the scope is realistic.

translationPractice.prompt: 你能在周四前帮我看一下建议部分吗？
translationPractice.answer: Could you review the recommendation before Thursday?
translationPractice.why: 指出要看的具体部分和截止时间。

translationPractice.prompt: 我很希望听听你对工作范围是否现实的意见。
translationPractice.answer: I’d value your feedback on whether the scope is realistic.
translationPractice.why: 说明希望同事评估范围是否现实。

translationPractice.prompt: 这些依据能支持这项建议吗？
translationPractice.answer: Does the evidence support the recommendation?
translationPractice.why: 检查现有依据能否支持建议，而不只是请同事润色。

choice.prompt: 同事请你读一份提案，最明确的请求是哪一条？
options: Can you look at this sometime?
Could you review the customer problem and recommendation by Thursday? I’d value your feedback on the scope.
choice.why: 第二种说法说明了要看的内容、时间和反馈重点。

output.prompt: 你准备周五提交客户方案，但价格假设尚未经过财务检查。请邀请财务同事先看价格部分，并询问这些假设是否足以支持报价。
output.sample: Could you review the pricing assumptions before Friday? I’d value your feedback on whether the current cost estimates support the proposed quote.
check: 明确请对方检查价格假设
询问依据是否支持报价
